To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) enhanced OECD TG 417 detects endocrine effects with 10-20 animals per sex per group; (2) medium-term liver and multi-organ carcinogenesis studies can be used to detect carcinogens and carcinogenic modifiers within a few months; and (3) the enhanced one-generation reproductive study is a promising protocol that needs further investigation.

(i) the enhanced TG 407 is a sensitive and useful assay for the detection of endocrinologically active chemicals; (ii) the medium-term carcinogenic assay can be applied for the detection of carcinogenic and modifying potential of endocrine active chemicals; and (iii) the one-generation reproduction assay can be used to detect endocrine disrupting chemicals that affect female fertility and offspring development.

(i) the enhanced OECD TG407 protocol detects endocrine active compounds, (ii) the medium-term rat carcinogenicity assays detect carcinogenic and non-carcinogenic effects of compounds with endocrine activity, (iii) the one-generation reproduction protocol detects endocrine effects of compounds on fertility and offspring.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of endocrine disrupting chemicals and with the development of appropriate test methods.
the development of simple, rapid, and reliable assays for conventional definite endocrine disruptor testing.
the development and evaluation of rapid, cost-efficient assays to identify endocrine active compounds and to assess the risk to humans and wildlife.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the enhanced OECD TG407 is a useful tool for detection of endocrine active effects of chemicals and that the enhanced one-generation reproduction assay is a promising tool for detection of reproductive effects of endocrine active chemicals.
the enhanced OECD TG407 and the medium-term rat carcinogenicity assays have been shown to detect effects of endocrine active chemicals.
the enhanced OECD TG is a useful tool for the characterization of the endocrine activity of a compound.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a number of simple, rapid and inexpensive assays are available to detect endocrine active compounds and to characterize their mode of action and hazard.

the use of the existing OECD TG 407 and the development of the enhanced OECD TGs are the most promising tools for the detection of endrocrine active chemicals in vivo, and that they should be used in the first step for the characterization of new chemicals with suspected endocrine activity.
the use of these protocols will provide a rapid and sensitive tool for the characterization of the endocrine active potential of a chemical.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current OECD TGs 421 and 414 should be revised and that a new TG for the one-generation reproduction assay should be established.

the OECD test guidelines for the detection of endogenous active compounds are well established and can be used in an appropriate manner to detect endocrine activity in a timely manner and to provide a solid scientific basis for risk assessment of endocrine active chemicals.
the use of a limited number of animals in a well designed study is sufficient to detect effects of endocrine disruptors.
